findings.explanation: retry_count = 0 tells Cloud Scheduler to never retry a failed invocation — the job simply waits for the next scheduled run. That's the API default, but here it sits alongside max_backoff_duration, max_doublings and min_backoff_duration, which only have any effect when retry_count > 0. As written, those three fields are inert and the block reads as if retries were intended but accidentally left disabled. Given the default schedule is weekly ("0 9 * * 1"), a single transient failure (Cloud Run cold start, IAM propagation delay, brief API blip) means the backup is silently skipped for a full week with no automatic recovery.
findings.fix:
retry_config {
  max_backoff_duration = "3600s"
  max_doublings        = 5
  max_retry_duration   = "0s"
  min_backoff_duration = "5s"
  retry_count          = 3
}
findings.remediation:
If retries are wanted (the backoff fields suggest they are), set retry_count to a small positive value, e.g. 3:

  retry_config {
    retry_count           = 3
    max_backoff_duration  = "3600s"
    max_doublings         = 5
    max_retry_duration    = "0s"
    min_backoff_duration  = "5s"
  }

If zero retries is actually intentional, remove the now-misleading backoff fields instead so the config doesn't imply retry behavior that isn't there.
findings.title: Cloud Scheduler retry_config.retry_count = 0 makes the configured backoff policy dead code

findings.explanation: The job template sets no `timeout`, so it falls back to Cloud Run's default of 600s (10 minutes). Cloud Run v2 Jobs support up to 24h, precisely because job workloads like table backups can run long — but this module gives callers no variable to raise it. A Bigtable backup that takes longer than 10 minutes (a realistic scenario for larger tables) is silently terminated mid-run by Cloud Run itself, not by an application error, so it may not surface clearly in logs.
findings.fix:
variable "timeout" {
  type        = string
  description = "Execution timeout for the backup job (e.g. \"3600s\"). Cloud Run Jobs default to 600s if unset, which may be too short for large Bigtable backups; max is 24h."
  default     = "3600s"
}

# in google_cloud_run_v2_job.tf, template.template block:
timeout = var.timeout
findings.title: Cloud Run v2 Job has no execution timeout configured or exposed, defaulting to 600s

findings.explanation: The only `required_providers`/`required_version` declaration in this repo lives in example/examplea/terraform.tf, which pins the consuming example, not the module itself. The module root (main.tf, google_cloud_run_v2_job.tf, google_cloud_scheduler.tf, google_service_account.tf) has no terraform {} block at all, so it places no floor on the Terraform CLI version or the hashicorp/google provider version a caller uses. A caller could apply this module with an old Terraform CLI or an incompatible google provider major version and get silently different behavior (e.g. google_cloud_run_v2_job attribute defaults have changed across provider majors), with no version-constraint error to catch it. Existing holden policies (HLD_TF_002/042/044/054) only fire once a terraform {} block exists and is misconfigured — they don't catch a block that's missing entirely.
findings.title: Root module has no terraform { } block — no required_version or required_providers constraint
